text_blocks.snippet: Scammers in Central Illinois frequently target residents using fake phone calls, phishing texts, and door-to-door repair cons.

list.snippet: Imposter Law Enforcement and Court Calls: Scammers spoof local numbers or federal agencies, claiming you missed a court date or owe fines that must be paid via Bitcoin or cash to avoid arrest. Courts and sheriff's offices never demand payment or bond money over the phone.

Fake DMV and Toll Texts: Fraudulent text messages claim you owe money for traffic tickets, tolls, or face driver's license suspension. Official state agencies do not request fine payments or sensitive data via text links.
Storm-Chasing Contractors: After severe weather, unverified door-to-door workers offer quick home repairs or free inspections. They often demand large upfront cash deposits and lack local permits.
Tech Support and AI Impersonators: Con artists use artificial intelligence to mimic family members or tech support, creating false emergencies that demand immediate wire transfers or gift cards.
Hang up and verify: Never act on urgent demands for money or personal data given over an incoming call. Look up the official number yourself to confirm.
Do not click links: Avoid opening links found in unsolicited text messages or emails regarding packages, tolls, or taxes.
Check contractor credentials: Always ask for local permits and written estimates before hiring repair services, and never pay the full price upfront.
Report fraud: File complaints with local law enforcement or submit a report to the Federal Trade Commission.
